messages:
tj: Quick sync — thinking out loud about a 'waveform' approach to continuous batching. Instead of fixed coalesce windows, we let per-tenant request intensity produce a short-lived waveform that informs admission and join/leave handshake. low-latency spikes get a narrow waveform, steady traffic gets a wide one. TL;DR: adaptive window shapes, not just sizes.
maya: interesting. how would we surface waveform boundaries to the scheduler? i worry about chattiness and oscillation. :thinking_face:
tj: Good point. my rough idea: each tenant has a lightweight pulse stream (an integer intensity + decay timestamp). Admission consults pulse to pick a waveform param set. joins are allowed if their predicted sample won't violate the waveform's expected latency budget. pulses decay on inactivity, so we avoid needing global timers.
sam: can we reuse existing lease tokens? or is this a parallel signal?
tj: Reuse where possible. Lease token remains the admission permit; waveform is advisory for batching windows and prefetch hints. If waveform suggests 'narrow fast window', leases get shorter timeouts and prefer fastpath packing. If wide, we relax deadlines and group more.
lina: how do we prevent attackers/rogue tenants from oscillating their pulses to game batching and starve others?
tj: rate-limit pulse updates per tenant (e.g., 1/s) and require pulse amplitude to be backed by observed recent qps. pulses not matching telemetry are downgraded. also global smoothing to avoid rapid switches.
maya: operationally, what metrics do we need to be able to debug waveform decisions?
sam: at minimum: tenant_pulse_amplitude, pulse_decayed_at, waveform_shape_id, join_attempts, join_success_rate, observed_batch_latency_p95, batch_fill_ratio.
infra-bot: deploy-checklist: add metrics + small feature flag. remember to update alerting runbook if waveform misfires.
tj: For APIs, admission path needs: consultPulse(tenant) -> Waveform {shape_id, window_ms, max_join_size, deadline_bias}. Keep consult cheap (inline memcache).
lina: Any changes to KV-cache warmup semantics? if we shrink windows for fast spikes we might increase cache churn.
tj: Yes — waveform should carry a warmup_hint flag (none | prefetch | conservative). For narrow windows we set conservative (skip expensive warmups). For wide windows we prefetch. Also add an eviction_threshold tweak per waveform to avoid thrash.
maya: code sketch?
tj: ```go
// consult in hot path
wf := pulseTable.Consult(tenantID)
if wf.Shape == Narrow {
  lease.Timeout = 8ms
  batch.Target = min(8, request.MaxTokens)
  warmup = Conservative
}
```
sam: Love the sketch. Two questions: 1) telemetry overhead of pulseTable. Consult is memcached-ish; 2) how to test fallbacks if pulse service is down?
tj: 1) design for L1 cache in-process and fallback to a sharded in-mem store; wire to existing admission cache. 2) fallback: if pulse missing -> default conservative waveform (safe). feature flag controls fulldev rollout.
lina: rollout plan? we should dogfood on a single cluster slice, enable for low-risk tenants first, and run chaos tests toggling pulses.
maya: also add an A/B where we force old-window semantics to compare latency/cost per tenant over 48h.
tj: Agreed. Ops checklist: feature flag gate, metrics + dashboard, canary tenants, automatic revert if batch_latency_p99 spikes > 2x baseline, and a mitigation to pin tenant to old admission manually.
sam: corner case: long-running chat streams where intensity oscillates but latency requirement stays high — waveform narrow->wide flips could hurt end-user UX. maybe add sticky hysteresis per session id.
tj: good call. add session_stickiness: once waveform chosen for a session, keep it for X minutes unless explicit break. make X tunable.
infra-bot: note: remember RBAC for pulse injector endpoints; don't expose to external SDKs.
lina: anything on observability traces? we should tag span with waveform_shape_id and pulse_version to correlate batch metrics back to decisions.
maya: yep. Add a small eval harness that replays production traces through the waveform logic to estimate savings before rollout.
tj: next steps: I'll write an RFC doc with shape taxonomy (spike, ramp, sustained), waveform encoding, pulse rate-limits, and fallback invariants. I'll include the Go sketch + memcache fallback and a minimal dashboard template. I'll ping owners for the metrics and canary list.
sam: ack. happy to help with chaos tests.
maya: ack. please add the session_stickiness and warmup_hint bits to the RFC.
infra-bot: scheduled: rfc-draft created in #eng-runtime tomorrow 10:00 UTC.
